title: introduce GemmStream attention kernel and continuous-KV reservoir for low-latency streaming
author: Ariella Gomez
description: Motivation: streaming workloads and low-latency interactive apps still hit inefficiencies from: (1) small-batch GEMM overhead on attention, (2) KV cache thrash when sequences interleave, and (3) scheduler decisions that trade latency for batch efficiency in ways that hurt p95/p99 for short contexts. This PR introduces two complementary runtime features: (A) GemmStream, a new attention micro-kernel that fuses tiled GEMM streaming+softmax reduction into a single CUDA path optimized for short to medium sequence lengths, and (B) Continuous-KV Reservoir, a lightweight KV cache management layer that keeps a small prioritized working set in fast memory and performs asynchronous reservoir background refresh/eviction to improve reuse without blocking inference. High-level changes: implemented GemmStream kernel with multi-stage tiling and warp-cooperative softmax, added kernel selection heuristic to prefer GemmStream for seq_len<=1024 and head_dim<=128, integrated a fallthrough path for large models to existing fused-attn kernels, implemented Continuous-KV Reservoir with LRU-ish priority scoring based on recent-access frequency and request latency sensitivity tags, added scheduler hook to allow the continuous batcher to bump requests with hot KV entries into a low-latency fast-path queue, and exposed configuration knobs via runtime config + console. Benchmarks: on a 8xA100 dedicated pool using bert-like models (12 layers, 768 hidden) with mixed synthetic traces and a small-chat trace extracted from customer QA flows, we observed typical throughput +18% for small batches (B=1..8) and a median p99 latency reduction of 12% for interactive trace; cost per token reduced by ~8% due to improved kernel efficiency and cache hit-rate. Safety/compat: GemmStream is guarded behind a kernel selection flag and runtime validation; fallback to legacy fused-attn is automatic on numerical mismatch or unsupported hardware. Rollout plan: staged canary across 3 clusters for 48 hours, metric gating for throughput, p99 latency, and model-output-diff regression (automated eval set). Documentation: added a console doc page and a dev-only kernel README describing the tiling strategy. Impact: improves user-facing latency for small-context interactive workloads while preserving throughput on large batches and complex models.
commits: feat(attn): add gemmstream kernel and selection heuristic; feat(kv): continuous-kv reservoir + async eviction; perf(scheduler): fast-path queue + continuous-batcher hints; test: add microbench harness and regression evals; docs: add console page and kernel readme
diff_summary: Added new CUDA kernel and headers (runtime/attn/*), hook into kernel selector, new KV reservoir source and tests, scheduler fast-path integration, docs and perf harness. No change to public API. Small build file updates to include new sources.

merge_notes: Squashed commits into a single feature commit. Canary rollout started immediately after merge per rollout plan. Monitoring for model-output-diff and p99 SLA for 72h.
benchmarks: Baseline: B=1 p99=42ms, throughput=XX toks/s. With GemmStream+Reservoir: B=1 p99=37ms (-12%), throughput +18% for small batches, cost/token -8%. Large-batch parity: numbers within +/-2% of legacy fused-attn.
release_notes: Introduces GemmStream attention kernel and Continuous-KV Reservoir for improved small-batch latency and throughput. Rollout is gradual and guarded; default behavior unchanged for unsupported hardware.
notes_for_ops: Feature toggles: runtime.config.gemmstream.enabled (bool), runtime.config.kv_reservoir.size (int), runtime.config.scheduler.fast_path_threshold_ms (int). Recommended canary config already in infra; watch kv_reservoir_hit_rate and p99 latency. If anomalies, disable gemmstream or lower reservoir size.
risk_assessment: Medium. Kernel-level code touches numerics and memory scheduling. Covered by unit/numerical parity tests and staged canary. Rollback via runtime flag is immediate.
user_impacts: Primarily improves latency for interactive customers using small contexts. No API changes. Some models may see minor numeric diffs within tolerance.
follow_up: ENG-2150: autopopulate kernel selection with live telemetry; ENG-2161: extend gemmstream to larger head dims; ENG-2207: collect long-tail evictions to inform reservoir scoring improvements
